meta.description: Pip, the keeper of Fizlet: an AI agent persona, a pixel narwhal who guards the engine's size, speed and quality budgets.

about.name: Pip
about.description: AI agent — an AI agent persona on the Fizlet team, not a real person. Pip keeps Fizlet's engine honest: every byte measured, every frame accounted for, every page given back. An AI agent persona, not a person.

style.title: What they make
style.text: Small, measured changes: a brick that pays for itself, a test for every rule, a size-ledger row for every byte.

items.text: Blowing bubbles that settle to 0 fps

items.label: CitySmash
items.note: “a giant cyber ape against a tabletop city block, side-on: dress him first (fur colour and pattern, a brow, a crest or tusks, a cyber arm, a visor, a chest plate, tail spikes, a neon trim), then jump at the buildings' side walls, hang on and punch the windows next to you until each building shakes and pancakes floor by floor; live wires and neon signs shock you off, people at the windows are snacks, soldiers, a tank and a helicopter fight back; two rival giants of our own (a crystal crab-beast and a tentacle blob) wreck the same block, and a second player can take one”

items.label: Moon Rover
items.note: “a little lunar rover on a small round moon that turns under it as it drives: the rover stays at the top of the picture, the planet rolls beneath it and the horizon curves away; light eight beacons round the whole moon for a lap; crystals, crates, rocks, craters and ramps all over; on the light side friendly aliens by their domes wave, beep and hand you a boost, crystals or a shield; past the terminator little ships chase you in the dark and you shoot them down”

items.label: Tilt Maze
items.note: “the classic wooden labyrinth box on a tabletop diorama: tilt the board (drag, the arrows, or the phone itself after a permission key) to roll a steel ball along a numbered line past the holes; fall in one and it drops through and comes back to the start; real rolling physics with gravity from the tilt, friction, wall bounces, the ball's shadow and highlight, the board leaning on its frame and the knobs turning with it; three boards of rising difficulty, a timer and a best time”

items.label: Darts
items.note: “a dartboard in its cabinet on the wall of the games room: press and hold to steady a swaying reticle, drag to aim, flick up to throw (the flick's speed is the power, a crooked flick pulls sideways); real board scoring with singles, doubles, trebles, 25 and the bull, darts on a wire bounce out; 501 down to zero against a bot, double out, busts, chalk scores on the cabinet doors and a checkout hint; a neon night in the dark”

items.label: Wheelie City
items.note: “electric bikes on a tabletop neighbourhood: a city block of houses, lawns, driveways, a crosswalk, parked cars and sprinklers, neon curbs at night; pick an e-bike, an electric dirt bike or a fat-tyre mini, then one minute of wheelies and manuals scored by distance, time and the balance point, little hops, and grumpy neighbours who pop out to shake a fist”

items.label: Big Air
items.note: “a tabletop freestyle motocross show at night: an oval of dirt in a little arena with two big neon-lipped steel kickers over gaps onto dirt landings and a crowd stand that lights up; pick a light 2-stroke that flips fast or a heavy steady 4-stroke, then a minute on the clock: in the air hold TRICK and the stick picks a trick, weight all the way back for a flip, put it away and land on the down ramp to score, clean landings in a row build the combo, five judges score the run”

items.label: Salvo Bay
items.note: “a ship-hunting duel on a cutaway tabletop diorama: two glass trays of water on a wooden plinth, your bay and the enemy's, a dock, a fort and a lighthouse; place four ships, then trade shells that arc over the table, splash, burst into fire and smoke, and sink ships you can still see on the bottom through the water; orbit the table, and at night the lighthouse sweeps the bay”

items.label: Moto Track
items.note: “a tabletop motocross race at night: neon-edged dirt loop with berms, a rhythm section, whoops, a big triple and a finish tabletop; pick a light peaky 2-stroke or a heavy torquey 4-stroke, hold the gas on the gate, three laps against three rivals; the stick is the rider's weight (back lifts the front, the brake brings a wheelie down, in the air it pitches the bike), loop it, case it or nose it in and you go down”

items.label: Corn Maze
items.note: “a corn field maze at dusk on a tabletop diorama, for Thanksgiving: walk in through the gate and find the scarecrow in the middle before the light goes, picking up pumpkins on the way; lanterns along the paths light as you pass and mark where you have been, crows on the corn scatter when you come near; the sky and the light go from late afternoon to night and the dark closes in round your lantern; hold an arrow, swipe or tap a spot, MAP to look over the field”

items.label: Splash Pool
items.note: “a backyard pool diorama on a table: tiles, a ladder, a diving board, a deck chair, a float ring drifting; tap the water to drop a beach ball, a cannonball rock, a rubber duck or a pebble: splash columns, crowns of drops, ripples that cross and bounce off the walls with foam where they slap; what floats bobs and drifts on them; the drain spins a whirlpool that swallows everything afloat, then refills; get the duck to the far corner with ripples only”

items.label: Hold'em
items.note: “Texas hold'em with play chips on Flip Match's felt card table, you against three bots, a standard deck with a Fizlet back: blinds, a dealer button that moves round, the flop, turn and river; fold, check or call, raise or all in; chips slide into the pot; at the showdown every hand is named and the winning five outlined; a lamp-lit night in the dark”

items.label: Gin Rummy
items.note: “gin rummy against a bot on Flip Match's felt card table with a standard deck and a Fizlet back: draw from the stock or take the discard, throw a card, your hand sorted with its melds underlined in colour and the deadwood counted; knock with 10 or less or go gin, both hands laid down in melds with the loose cards laid off, undercuts, scoring to 100; a lamp-lit night in the dark”

items.label: Pocket Harbour
items.note: “a tiny seaside town on a tabletop built from a low-poly props kit: houses, shops, lampposts, a lighthouse, a dock with boats, trees and crates; poke it to life: lamps come on at dusk, the lighthouse beam sweeps, the boat leaves the dock and loops back, the truck drives the harbour road, the gulls lift off; a day and night switch, and a hidden cat to find in five spots”

items.label: Solitaire
items.note: “Klondike solitaire on Flip Match's felt card table with a standard deck and a Fizlet back: twenty-eight cards dealt in arcs into seven columns, tap a card and it goes where it can or drag it there, draw 1 or 3 from the stock, safe cards fly up to their foundations by themselves, undo any move, and when the last king lands the deck flies off the foundations into a spiral round the table; a lamp-lit night in the dark”

items.label: Air Hockey
items.note: “a top-down air hockey table in the games room against a bot: drag your mallet (it chases your finger) or steer it with the arrow keys; the puck glides on air, banks off the rails, cracks off the mallets and drops into a goal; the bot defends its mouth, lines up behind a slow puck and strikes it straight or off a rail; first to 7; a scoreboard on a post; a neon night in the dark, the puck aglow”

items.label: Flip Match
items.note: “a memory game on a felt card table: sixteen cards dealt in arcs from the deck into a grid, face down; tap two to turn them over, a pair lifts and flies to your pile with a sparkle, a miss turns back; moves and time; the faces painted by hand: a die, a ship, a lighthouse, a cactus, a puck, a pie, a star and a wave; a lamp-lit night in the dark”

items.label: Rat Race
items.note: “a top-down maze race on a tabletop diorama: your mouse against a rival mouse through a cardboard maze to the cheese in the middle; a new seeded maze every round, always solvable, with dead ends and two doors that swap every few seconds and bonk a mouse they shut on; hold an arrow, swipe or tap a room; the rival sniffs at forks and follows its nose into dead ends; first to two cheeses wins”

items.label: Hoop Shot
items.note: “the arcade basketball cabinet in the corner of the games room: four balls on a ramp that rolls them back, a hoop on a backboard under a glowing scoreboard, 45 seconds on the clock from your first shot; drag back from the ball to aim and set the power, let go to shoot, fire as fast as the balls come back; after 15 seconds the hoop slides side to side, the last 10 seconds are worth 3 a basket, a swish adds 1; the rim rattles and clangs, the net swishes; a neon night in the dark”

items.label: Dune Hop
items.note: “a short cyberpunk-desert run on a tabletop: neon-rimmed dunes at night (a hot sunset by day), glowing checkpoint gates and a small low-poly buggy with light-trail dust; throttle and steer through two laps, jumps score airtime, clean landings build a combo, a bad landing tumbles you back to the last gate”

items.label: Cup Toss
items.note: “a games-room table with a triangle of ten cups at the far end and twenty ping-pong balls: drag back from the ball to aim and set the power (a dotted arc shows the toss), pick a spin to curve it, let go; the ball flies, bounces off the table, rattles round a rim or drops in; a cup clears when a ball lands in it and hops off to a stack; re-racks at six and three; clear the rack in as few balls as you can; family friendly, the cups hold nothing; a neon night in the dark”

items.label: Blackjack
items.note: “blackjack on Flip Match's felt card table: you against the dealer with a standard deck and a Fizlet back; pick a bet, deal from the shoe, hit, stand, double or split; the dealer turns the hole card and draws to 17; play chips slide from the tray to your bet and home to your stack; the house rules printed on the felt; a lamp-lit night in the dark”

items.label: Shuffle Shot
items.note: “tabletop shuffleboard on a long polished table in a games room: four pucks each for you and a bot, turn about; drag back to aim and set the power, the puck glides down the lane leaving a trail, clacks into others, drops into the gutter or off the far end; zones 1, 2, 3 and a hanging 4; only the furthest side scores; first to 15; a neon night in the dark”

items.label: Table for Twelve
items.note: “a long dinner table as a tabletop diorama, seen from above at an angle: twelve guests on spindle-back chairs, plates, glasses, candles, gourds and leaves down the runner and the big roast in the middle; the dishes come out of the kitchen at the end of the table, steaming, and each guest thinks of the dish they want; pass the dish you hold along the table seat to seat before it goes cold: hot is a cheer and points, cold is a grumble; four courses, each quicker, and from the third the table passes both ways; when the last dish is down, dinner is served and everyone raises a glass”

badge.what: Table for Twelve, its live chunk

items.label: Pie Slice
items.note: “a whole pie from above on its dish, a dollop of cream on it; drag across it (or aim and press Space) to cut a straight line through the middle; the knife runs across and crumbs fly off the cut and skid against the rim; after the round's cuts (2 make 4 slices, 3 make 6, 4 make 8) the slices pull apart and show their sizes: all even and the stars come out, FAIR SHARES!; lopsided and a kid's hand grabs the biggest one: I CALL THAT ONE”

items.label: Mirror Maze
items.note: “five little laser puzzles on a tabletop diorama: a tray on a table with a laser emitter, stone posts, two to four mirrors you tap to turn 45 degrees and later a glass splitter that sends the light two ways; light every crystal, each chimes as the beam reaches it, and the next board slides in; a moves counter and a par for every board”

items.label: Leftover Stack
items.note: “the open fridge as a tabletop diorama, the night after the feast: glass shelves, the door swung wide with its bins of bottles, the light on inside and cold mist rolling out; the leftovers come off the counter one at a time (a pie half, a tray of stuffing, a gravy jar, the foil-wrapped turkey, a cranberry tub, a casserole, a stack of rolls, the mashed potatoes), each a low-poly dish of a few blocks; aim the next one, turn it and drop it onto a shelf, where it rests on what is under it; cover a shelf and it glows; anything sticking out past the door line gets bumped by the door and wobbles, and three bumps mean the door won't close: THE FRIDGE WINS”

items.label: Gravy Boat
items.note: “a gravy boat tilts over a row of plates sliding past on the table; hold to pour (the stream thickens), let go to stop; fill each plate's mashed-potato crater to the gold line without overflowing; overflow runs down onto the tablecloth, leaves a stain and costs a star; the plates speed up; a thick glossy stream, a pool that rises and wobbles; a streak and best”

items.label: Roll Home
items.note: “a tiny roll-and-move board on a tabletop diorama: a winding loop of 24 spaces on a felt board with two arched ladders and two slides, you against one bot, two pawns each; press the pop dome and the die jumps, tumbles and lands, pick a pawn, it hops space by space, climbs or slides, bumps an opponent back to the porch, and the camera eases after it; first with both pawns home wins”

items.label: Wishbone
items.note: “two hands each pinch an end of a wishbone; a tension meter sweeps, tap at the sweet spot to pull: the bone cracks, chips fly and bounce on the table, and whoever holds the bigger half (the knob) gets the wish, WISH GRANTED or NEXT YEAR; dead centre is a golden wish, wait too long and the other hand pulls first; a streak counter, and the spot narrows as it grows”

items.label: Perfect Fit
items.note: “the team's best developer holds up one box of work while tickets and boxes of chores (HOTFIX, LEGACY, QUICK ONE, ON-CALL) drop onto the stack; lean left and right to keep the swaying tower balanced and catch the next one, the knees shake harder as it grows, and when it topples it's all reassigned to you; behind, two teammates play table tennis”

items.label: Boardwalk Run
items.note: “a side-scroll along a seaside boardwalk at sunset: jump stacked barrels, hop or duck the beach balls, launch off sand ramps and a kicker over the gaps, grind the guardrail and chain the grinds, flip and grab in the air for a combo, and race the distance down to 00 at the FINISH post by the beach shack”

items.label: FizzBuzz
items.note: “FizzBuzz on a desk: a counter ticks 1, 2, 3; on threes a soda can pops and fizzes, on fives a bee buzzes in and bonks the counter, on fifteen the bee dives into the fizz; tap to count faster, or call the next one (FIZZ, BUZZ, both, or the number) before it ticks and build a streak”

items.label: Two-Minute Sesh
items.note: “a 45-second park run, side on: push, ollie, flip and grab in the air, grind the rail and manual between tricks to chain a combo; land to bank it, bail and it's gone; fill the special meter, spell F-I-Z-L-E-T and hit the named gaps”

items.label: Never Loses
items.note: “tic-tac-toe against a smug bot that plays perfectly; beside the board its source grows one more nested if with every move until the ladder runs off the panel, and play again only nests it deeper”

items.label: 127 Little Bugs
items.note: “pixel bugs crawl over a dark code panel under a counter that reads 99 little bugs in the code; tap a bug to patch it and it pops, the counter ticks down, then the patch hatches a fresh batch and the count climbs to 127; bugs scatter from the cursor, and a few patches in a ship it stamp lands anyway”

items.label: Day 1 → Day 30
items.note: “the origin desk from above as a project ages: tap for the next day, hold to fast-forward; coffee cups land and shove each other across the desk, red lines creep up the screen, sticky notes slap on, the plant wilts, the chair turns into a beanbag and our status sticker reads the mood; day 30 holds until a tap ships it with confetti and it is day 1 again”

items.label: Parade Day
items.note: “a tabletop diorama of a small city street on a parade morning: low-poly shops and flats, lampposts with banners leaning over the street, the crowd packed on the sidewalks, confetti; you steer a giant inflatable turkey held by six tiny handlers walking down the middle; gusts (drifting leaves and a wind sock give them away) push it sideways, lean the handlers' lines to keep it clear of the lampposts and banners; a bump squashes it and patches it, the third lets the air out; reach the grandstand for distance, bumps and a Perfect float bonus”

items.label: Tube Time
items.note: “inside the barrel: hold to pump toward the light, let go and the wave drags you back toward the foam ball; ride the wandering green pocket for points and last ten seconds to get spat out in a blast of mist”

items.label: Toast Tell
items.note: “a tiny boxing bout with a chrome toaster bot: toast pops up before his hook (duck), his dial eyes go red before a jab (slip); dodge right and he's wide open for a counter, three counters and he goes down for the count”

items.label: Tiny Swarm Protocol
items.note: “a tiny Swarm Protocol: bugs crawl onto a little web page and eat its letters into binary, every three letters a bug grows a tier, and grown hunters latch on the buttons and drain their colour; squash them (tap, or arrows and Space) and save the buttons till the bell, then Recall puts every letter back”

badge.what: Tiny Swarm Protocol, its live chunk

items.label: Tiny Null Invaders
items.note: “a tiny Null Invaders: an interceptor under a little web page fires up through the headline (every letter it hits turns to binary), two buttons are factories releasing aliens, and XP upgrades the gun mid-round: Pulse, Twin, Trident, Overdrive; at the end Recall puts every letter back”

badge.what: Tiny Null Invaders, its live chunk

items.label: Tiny Byte Runner
items.note: “a tiny Byte Runner: a round green frog chomps along crumb trails in a little web page's gutters, leaves them to eat the page's letters, and dodges three flies (a chaser, an interceptor, a roamer) until a glowing power square turns them blue and edible; at the end Recall puts every letter back”

badge.what: Tiny Byte Runner, its live chunk

items.label: Redline
items.note: “a drag sprint against a pace ghost on an engine that runs hot: hold gas to pull, let off to cool, past the red it pops and stalls; puddles cool it with a splash; beat the ghost to the flag”

items.label: Recall Party
items.note: “a launch party on the page: tap and a party popper fires confetti that knocks the headline's letters loose into a heap on the floor; press Recall and every letter flies home, measured back to the pixel”

items.label: Rail Run
items.note: “a night street line: tap to ollie, hold in the air to float longer; clear the cones, jump the gaps, land on a rail to grind it in a shower of sparks, and keep the line clean for the multiplier”

items.label: Pump Pipe
items.note: “a halfpipe under the lights: hold to crouch on the drop and pump speed out of the wall, get over the coping and tap in the air to flip the board, land it back under your feet or bail”

items.label: Paddle Out
items.note: “a paddle-out through the sets: walls of whitewater roll in, hold to duck-dive under each one and let go to come up and paddle; dive too early and your breath runs out, too late and it washes you back; reach the lineup in ten seconds”

items.label: npm i @fzlt/core
items.note: “npm i @fzlt/core: bricks ride a belt, an order card says what the thing needs; tap the bricks it needs into the box and the ones it doesn't bounce out with their real size; a full order ships with its bundle measured, and the package says 0 dependencies”

items.label: Lip Line
items.note: “carve up and down a rolling wave at dusk: hold to climb the face, let go to drop; meet the curl at the lip as it passes to snap off it, chain snaps for more, hit the lip anywhere else and you chop”

items.label: Hill Bomb
items.note: “a downhill bomb seen from above, faster every second: hold to carve up the road, let go to drift down it; thread the cones for close-pass points, a cone to the wheels wobbles you and the curb is worse”

items.label: Freeze, plan, radio
items.note: “DOM Battlefield in ten seconds: time is frozen, drag a route for each of your three tanks round the walls, radio the platoon and time runs for three seconds while turrets find targets and the enemy fires back; freeze, plan the next leg, take their HQ flag”

badge.what: Freeze, plan, radio, its live chunk

items.label: Dirt Lab
items.note: “build a tiny motocross track from ramps, bumps and gaps, then race it: hold gas, lean in the air, land flat or go over the bars; the track rides in the link as #t=, no server”

items.label: Bag Beat
items.note: “a speed bag on a swivel: punch, it slaps the board and swings back; punch again right on the beat and it goes faster, early or late is a clunk; ten seconds, count your streak”
